title: Amantu billahi – belief in Allah (SWT)
intro: The first pillar of Iman: Allah is the One Creator and Ruler of everything.

learn.text: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

learn.html: Allah (SWT) is the Lord and Creator of everything – One and Only, with no partner, and nothing is equal to Him. In the Qur’an Allah described Himself in the most beautiful and perfect way, by mentioning His attributes (sifat) and His most beautiful names (al-asma’ al-husna).

Allah is perfect, His attributes are perfect and His names are the most beautiful. Through them we know and believe in Allah – both in the description of His being (as-sifat adh-dhatiyyah) and in the description of His perfection (as-sifat ath-thubutiyyah).

learn.label: The best part of Iman
learn.en: There is no god except Allah.

learn.html: We express our belief in Allah with the words la ilaha illallah. In a hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) called this sentence the best part of Iman, because it both denies and affirms: it denies that any other god exists, and it affirms that there is only One God, Allah, with all His attributes.

learn.text: Allah is the Ruler and the Creator

learn.html: The first pillar of Iman also means believing that only Allah is the Creator and the Ruler. He created everything, and His creating never stops – there is no moment when Allah is not creating. We see new life being created in plants and in animals. He created everything we see with our eyes and with modern instruments, in the tiniest worlds and in the biggest.

learn.text: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging the matter [of His creation].
Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it.

learn.html: Our mind is also a way to know Allah: it makes us think about this world. Scientists have found many facts that point to Allah’s existence, and thinking people concluded that someone must have created the world and everything in it. Some call it a “creative force” – we believers know that it is Allah (SWT). He rules over everything we know and don’t know, see and don’t see.

‘Umar (RA) said: one day, while we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (SAW), a man in very white clothes with very black hair appeared. There was no sign of travel on him and none of us knew him. He sat in front of the Prophet (SAW), knee to knee, and asked him about Islam, Iman and Ihsan, and about the Last Day.

items: Islam is to testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad (SAW) is His Messenger, to pray, to give zakah, to fast in Ramadan and to go on Hajj if you are able.
Iman is to believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, the Last Day, and that everything – good and bad – is decreed.
Ihsan is to worship Allah as if you see Him – for even if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.

learn.html: Each time, the man said: “You have spoken the truth.” When he had left, the Prophet (SAW) said: “That was Jibril. He came to teach you your religion.” (Muslim)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: A Muslim lives by Allah’s mercy, and believing in Allah (SWT) is the natural state of every human being.

practice.title: Islam, Iman or Ihsan?
practice.prompt: In the hadith of Jibril, which one is this part of?

items.text: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him

practice.title: Match the words
pairs: There is no god except Allah
The angel who came to teach the religion

questions.q: How did Allah (SWT) describe Himself in the Qur’an?
options: With His attributes (sifat) and His most beautiful names

questions.q: Which words express our belief that Allah exists?
options: La ilaha illallah – there is no god except Allah
Alhamdulillah – all praise is for Allah

questions.q: Why is “la ilaha illallah” the best part of Iman?
options: It denies all other gods and affirms the One God, Allah
Because it is said only in Ramadan

questions.q: What does the first pillar of Iman include?
options: Believing that only Allah is the Creator and the Ruler
Believing only what we can see

questions.q: Who was the man in very white clothes in the hadith?

options: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him, knowing that He sees you
